author: ne valley times
title: HonorHealth launches institute focused on prevention and whole-person healthcare
text:
HonorHealth, a nonprofit healthcare system in the Phoenix area, has announced the launch of the HonorHealth Whole Health Institute. The new institute will focus on prevention, whole-person care, and evidence-based lifestyle interventions as part of its effort to address chronic disease and improve health outcomes.
According to data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, 60% of Americans live with at least one chronic disease. These conditions make up seven of the top ten causes of death in the country. While genetics play a role in about 30% of cases, most risk factors are linked to diet, stress, lifestyle choices, and social determinants of health.
The HonorHealth Whole Health Institute plans to combine evidence-based therapies with integrative and lifestyle medicine approaches. Its programs will include the Center for Culinary Medicine, Lifestyle Medicine Primary Care, Medical Fitness and Longevity Center, and Diabetes Center of Excellence.
“Launching the Whole Health Institute reflects HonorHealth’s commitment to moving beyond sick care toward true health and healing,” said Todd LaPorte, CEO of HonorHealth. “This institute will help us build innovative care models that empower patients, strengthen our communities, and advance our mission to improve the health and well-being of those we serve.”
The new institute aims to bring together clinical care, research initiatives, education efforts, and community engagement. Programs are designed as part of an ecosystem that supports healthier choices for patients over time.
“This is a unique opportunity to reimagine healthcare by placing prevention and well-being at the center of the patient experience,” said Shad Marvasti, M.D., Executive Director of the Whole Health Institute. “With support from colleagues, philanthropic partners and academic leaders, we can build sustainable, evidence-based models that improve health outcomes and build healthier communities across Arizona and beyond.”
HonorHealth will work with its foundation partners for funding support as well as collaborate with Arizona State University on education and research related to integrative health.
More information about these initiatives can be found at wholehealth.honorhealth.com.
